post.description: To read an indicator's release history further back than the five rows event_detail returns; event_graph gives the same values as numbers for charting.

depth.description:
Show More step, cumulative: depth 1 is the first expansion (about 15 newest releases), each further step returns a longer prefix. Pass next_depth from the previous response to go deeper.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 50; default 1.

event_id.description:
Any release event id of the indicator (from list_events).

Provider reference: minimum 1.

200.description:
An indicator's release history (newest first) keyed by any of its release event ids: date, actual, forecast, previous, revision and the site's better/worse judgement. `depth` is the site's Show More step and is cumulative: each step returns a longer prefix of the same history (observed 15 rows at depth 1, 35 at 2, 65 at 3), so one call at the returned continuation depth supersedes the previous one; `has_more` says whether a deeper step exists.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `depth` | number | The Show More step this prefix corresponds to. |
| `event_count` | number |  |
| `event_id` | number |  |
| `events` | object[] |  |
| `has_data_values` | boolean |  |
| `has_more` | boolean | True when a deeper Show More step exists. Call again with depth set to next_depth; each step returns a longer prefix of the same history, not a new page. |
| `next_depth` | number | The depth to pass next to see older releases. Null when has_more is false or depth 50 (the maximum) was reached. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `source_url` | string |  |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

post.description: To see what is scheduled or was released in a date window, or to find an event_id to pass to event_detail, event_history or event_graph.

currencies.description: Keep only events of these currencies (the nine the site filters on). Default: all.

date.description: Anchor date, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today (UTC). Mutually exclusive with `start`/`end`. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

event_types.description: Keep only these site event-type categories. Default: all.

impacts.description: Keep only these impact levels (`holiday` is the site's Non-Economic grey level). Default: all.

start.description: Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD (requires `end`; at most 62 days inclusive). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

view.description:
Window around `date`: the day itself, the Sunday-to-Saturday week containing it, or its calendar month. Ignored when `start`/`end` are given.

Provider reference: allowed values ["day", "week", "month"]; default "week".

200.description:
List the economic calendar events of one day, week, month or custom date range (at most 62 days), optionally filtered by impact, currency and event type. Returns each event's identifiers, scheduled time (epoch seconds and UTC), impact, actual, forecast, previous and revision values as the site states them (empty values are null). Parsed from the calendar page's inline state (same data the site's calendar app renders).

The response contains the tool result directly.
